title: Previous Visitor
paragraphs: “Hmm… She’s got a good feel for it. Imia is dexterous, so she precisely hits the weak points of the monsters.”

After that, the battles in the dungeon continued. Since the recent battle had just ended, we were taking a short break. While we were resting, it wasn’t exactly a review session, but Ren was praising the mole.
“Y-Yes.”

“That’s true. She’s really good at striking the monsters’ eyes, between their eyebrows, the heart… and between the scales. She finishes them off even cleaner than the ones Ren and Motoyasu took down.”
“When dismantling them, you can really feel her skill. Even though she’s more like a disciple, there’s a lot to learn from her.”
“Uh, ah, u-uh…”
The mole is really shy. She couldn’t get any words out at all.
“Changing the subject, which is better, weapons dropped by monsters or custom-made ones?”
“Let’s try asking the craftsmen and blacksmiths in Faubley next time.”
“It’s like in a monster-hunting game where the weapons take on that kind of look, huh?”
“Even when using monster materials, it gives off that vibe.”
“Yeah, but being able to make different weapons from the same monster is an advantage, isn’t it?”

Father’s reasoning had a slightly complex nuance. If I were to compare it to Father from the first world, it would be like the armor he used to love. I think it was called the barbarian armor, which he gradually reinforced with various materials. In the case of the hero’s weapon, there are various types—directly from the monster, from materials, and from crafted weapons. To use a spear as an example… suppose there’s a spear made from dragon bones. In the case of the hero’s weapon, that would be the Dragon Bone Lance. By coating the handle with leather and attaching scales to improve durability, it becomes stronger. Furthermore, by adding high-magic-effect gems as accessories, the hero’s weapon has enhancements that can only be replicated through copying. By that point, it would likely be given a different weapon name.
“That’s true.”
“For Itsuki, maybe he could improve the grip with new materials or make bullets from monster materials?”
“His gun can shoot endlessly, so if he loads it with special bullets, wouldn’t that increase its power even more?”
“Adjusting the grip and fine-tuning it might make it even stronger.”
“Uh… Naofumi-san? I’m fine with strengthening my weapon, but what about yours?”
“Well, it’s a shield… it kind of just works by absorbing materials, you know?”
“Ah… I see. Sorry.”
“It’s fine, it’s fine. I can also synthesize the weapons I get for enhancements, so it’s not weak at all.”
Speaking of which, there’s a way to combine the traits of multiple weapons to enhance a weapon.
“Hero weapons just aren’t suited for fine-tuning. In that sense, having weapons custom-made gives another way to get stronger.”

“Basically, they become easier to handle and more user-friendly, but there’s always the issue of disliking the design or something. It would be great if we could refine it to fix those little things, like only being able to synthesize the primary feature with special effects.”
It seems Ren also had some thoughts about his sword. I’ve been using mine for so long that I’ve gotten used to it.
“If Imia is dexterous, it might be good to let her handle firearms as well. It depends on her abilities, but since she’s become quite strong, there shouldn’t be a problem.”
“In Itsuki’s case, with his high level and exceptional abilities, the bullet hits as soon as he fires. But for regular shooting, you can actually see the bullet.”
That’s true. It’s not so slow that it looks like it’s standing still, but with the enhanced status of a hero, you can see it and dodge it.
“As a hero, your abilities make it easier to judge with your eyes.”
“Um… well…”
“It’s fine, Imia. Just aim as if you’re using magic to precisely hit your target, and pull the trigger the same way you’d aim to strike a weak point with a short sword. You’ll hit your target.”
For some reason, Itsuki is giving the mole a lesson on handling firearms. It looks like we’re about to learn about parts of Itsuki’s abilities beyond his accuracy.
“Imia-chan is starting to feel like an all-around character.”
“She can do anything with ease.”
“Starting with magic, now she’s mastering swordsmanship… and she even helps Naofumi-san with cooking. Being dexterous really makes her versatile.”
“We need to be careful not to make her a jack-of-all-trades. Her footwork during battle is still a bit shaky. Even her swordsmanship hasn’t stood out yet.”
“Since a hero is teaching her one-on-one… it’d be great if she grows into an all-around talent.”
Father pats the mole on the head. The mole lowers her head even more, looking embarrassed. Father and the others smile warmly at the sight.
“…I’m not that confident in my sword technique either. Éclair is still better than me.”
“Even in my training with Motoyasu-san, our fights are still full of wasted movement. We’ll need to train even harder from now on.”
“That’s why I’ll be taking Imia’s thrusts as reference.”
“Constant improvement is key. I also need to think about positioning and how to block so I can defend against any attack.”
After those conversations wrapped up, Father spoke after a short break.
“Alright, it’s about time…”

With that, Father stood up and began walking again. Before long… we reached the exit of the complicated maze… According to Rival, it seemed like the entrance to the room where the dragon, likely the boss here, was waiting, came into view.
“Hm? What’s that…?”
“Huh?”
“What is it?”
When Father narrowed his eyes and pointed, we saw a figure entering the entrance.
“Is it a humanoid monster pulling strings from behind the scenes?”
“Doesn’t seem like it. Looked more like an adventurer who got here ahead of us.”
“There are adventurers who can make it this far, huh?”

Oh my, well, since it’s us, it feels like a field trip, but the monsters are quite strong. Given the level of monsters appearing here, this dungeon would be difficult for regular adventurers. Well, sometimes there are adventurers with exceptional combat abilities. They must have been lucky to make it this far.
“What should we do if there’s someone ahead of us?”
“They probably wouldn’t like it if we snatched their prey, so maybe we should just hide and observe for now?”
“Yeah. By the way, it’s easy to forget, but what do adventurers think about defeating the master of a dungeon like this?”
Father looks at Éclair. Éclair, perhaps not very knowledgeable about the rules of this country or about adventurers, waves her hand in front of her face. She probably doesn’t know.
“An unspoken rule among adventurers?”
“If the boss is defeated, the dungeon stops functioning… That would be a huge loss for adventurers who rely on monsters and treasure.”
“Whether it’s monsters or humans, both are subject to natural selection… It’s a question of whether it’s okay to destroy that environment.”
“I don’t think it’s a problem. If it’s a dungeon managed by a dragon, wouldn’t another dragon just take over the territory after it’s defeated?”
“That’s one way to think about it… But we’re getting off track. The point is, what should we do now that there’s someone ahead of us?”
Hearing Ren’s words, Father and the others cross their arms in thought.
“In online games, it’s proper etiquette to wait your turn…”
“But this isn’t about winning or losing. It’s life or death. Maybe we should just watch, and if it looks like they’re going to lose, we can help?”
“Still, isn’t it wrong to just wait and watch them get into trouble?”
“True. I’d rather not act like the version of me that Motoyasu-san talks about.”

“But if we defeat the boss, wouldn’t they accuse us of stealing their prey? Adventurers are after treasure and experience points, and if they’re challenging the dungeon boss, they should be fully prepared, right?”

This is a tricky problem. During the Cal Mira Island event, we knew how strong the adventurers were, so the deeper bosses were ignored. At that time, we changed which island we went to each day to avoid conflicts.
“In a way, it feels like the same issue as the friction between heroes.”
“That’s true. But letting them die because the boss is too strong seems wrong too.”
“They chose a dangerous life as adventurers and took on the dungeon boss. There’s no reason for us to interfere.”
“Hmm… It’s a tough call. If we defeat the boss, we might end up with a bad reputation.”
“It really depends on the situation. Like Motoyasu-san said, I’m not that version of myself, but it’s probably best to watch for now and only step in if things get dangerous.”
“Got it.”
“That’s reasonable.”

The plan was set. We would observe the adventurers from the shadows and step in to help if things looked bad. It might seem like we were hoping things would get dangerous, but it’s about respecting their intentions.
“Sakura-chan, Imia-chan, Windia-chan, and Gaelion-chan, you’re all probably tired, and you’ve done a great job, so no need to fight anymore.”
“That was fun!”
“It was a nice change of pace.”
“The maze was so much fun!”
Hearing the responses from the Filolials made me feel happy too.
“It was good practice for moving in tight spaces.”
“It was a good experience for providing support.”
“Ah… Yes. I gained some real combat experience. I’ll do my best to move better next time.”
Rival and the others gained a lot of experience too. Experience that can’t be measured by points… That’s a valuable asset.
“Éclair, if something happens, we’re counting on you to support us.”
“Understood. Hopefully, the adventurers ahead of us will defeat the boss.”
“Yeah. We might not get the boss’s treasure, but it wouldn’t be a wasted trip for us either.”
With that, we cautiously peeked through the door leading to the room where the dungeon master was supposedly waiting.
Chapter 686 – Spectating

It seems that a boss battle is about to begin in the room at the deepest part of the dungeon. At the far end of the large hall, a dragon was eagerly awaiting the arrival of intruders. The interior had a somewhat temple-like feel. As expected, the master managing the dungeon was a dragon. The adventurers preparing to fight… I don’t know them.
“Huh? Isn’t that adventurer…”
“That’s the group called Yuta, isn’t it? So they’ve made it this far.”
“Maybe they came to that town specifically to challenge this place?”
“If they made it this far, they must be quite skilled.”
We watched the battle unfold from a distance.
Ah! It was Cola. I had completely forgotten about them.
“We’ll take the treasure you possess! With that treasure—”
They seem to be exchanging words before the fight. The dragon, apparently intelligent, responded.
“The treasure that the master of this place holds?”
“Could it be a tool with powerful magical effects?”
“Ah, I’ve heard of it in legends. There’s a story about the item possessed by the master of this dungeon.”
Éclair added some information. Hmm, I want that treasure. I’ll make a name for myself and present it to Father. Cola, lose already.
“Hmm… well, that’s how it usually goes.”
And with that, the dragon roared in response to Cola’s words, surrounding them with its subordinates as the battle began.
“Boo!”
“Boop!”
“Buhee!”
“Let’s go!”
Well then, Cola, who was wielding a fancy sword not seen in town, started fighting the dragon.
“Ah, so they had a real weapon all along.”
“They probably hid their prized weapon and used a cheap one to avoid standing out and to fend off any adventurers who tried to pick a fight.”
“But if that draws trouble instead, isn’t it pointless? Trying not to stand out only to get dragged into more problems seems counterproductive.”

From what I can see, Cola’s party seems to have the upper hand. As for the dragon’s strength—since the space is confined, the troublesome aspects of a powerful dragon in the open are less of a concern. Instead, it seems like the enclosed space makes its breath attacks almost unavoidable. That’s what I was thinking, but Cola’s attacks are being deflected by the dragon’s scales.
“Are dragons that make dungeons their territory tougher than those living in mountains outside?”
“I think their scales are harder.”
“Isn’t it just individual differences? The room is wide enough, so it can still fly and dodge attacks, right?”
“Still… we’re sitting here watching all high and mighty.”
“Yeah… we shouldn’t be watching so casually like it’s a heartwarming scene…”
As we talked, we continued watching Cola’s battle.
“Ugh…! This sword isn’t working at all!”
That’s not true.
If you ask me, what do they expect to happen by swinging their sword at the dragon’s hard scales? If they don’t aim for the softer areas like the joints, eyes, or mouth, what are they even doing?
“Imea-chan, where would you aim?”
Father must have been thinking the same thing.
“Uh, um… the eyes or mouth… If that’s too hard, then the stomach…”
“That’s the correct answer.”
“Oh, and I’d use magic to weaken the rock ceiling and drop it on the dragon to restrict its movement.”
“If you can think that far ahead and act on it, then you pass.”
“Well, in that regard, they’re fighting in a pretty brute-force manner. Should we step in after the fight and lecture them?”
“Let’s not. We’d just come off as arrogant newcomers.”
“A world where we can’t even point out mistakes…”
“Itsuki, you’ve started making jokes too. You’re becoming more like Naofumi.”
“I’ll ask what that means later.”
And so, we continued observing Cola’s battle.
“Bububu.”
“Bububububu!”
“Buhee!”
At that moment, a pig-like creature that seemed to be one of Cola’s companions said something to them. Then, Cola distanced themselves from the dragon, leaving it to the pigs.
“They’re trying to set up some kind of finishing move. It looks like it’ll be flashy, like a special technique.”
“Eclair-san does that sometimes too, right? The move where she channels magic into her short sword and thrusts with it.”
“That’s not a skill, but a magic sword technique.”
“Indeed. It’s a special move that enhances power by infusing magic into the blade.”
“A finishing move… that sounds cool. I want to learn one too.”
“The Heroes already have skills for that.”
“Motoyasu-kun, did the ‘me’ from my first world have any special techniques?”
“You used moves like replicating the Air One-Way Shield without a skill and a technique to absorb enemy magic, I believe.”
“Oh, I see…”
Father looked slightly disappointed with my explanation.
It was strong enough that it couldn’t be underestimated, though? Since it could counterattack, Father was satisfied.
So why is there this difference?
“No matter how hard you try, I guess you really don’t have any offensive techniques, huh, Naofumi-san.”
“The only powerful attack method I have is to resort to using the cursed weapon…”
Ah, so that’s what’s been troubling Father.
“No problem! Father will learn powerful support magic, after all!”
“Was it Carmilla Island? Maybe I should go learn it as soon as possible.”
“Yeah. It might be a good idea to go after the next Wave, which is coming soon.”
“The activation is still a ways off.”
It’s only been a little over three weeks since the Wave in Melromarc.
There might be signs, but isn’t it still too soon?
“It’s not about leveling up, it’s about learning magic.”
“I heard the winds in that area are so complex that airships and planes can’t safely fly there.”
“Not to mention the floating rocks and stuff around there, making it hard for planes to fly.”
“Can Gaelion fly us there in one go?”
“Would a dragon be able to manage it? Either way, a ship might be safer… right?”
As we chatted, Cola shouted out and thrust both hands forward, summoning what looked like a magic sphere.
“Haaaaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhh!”
In the next instant, we were all stunned.
“Air St Throw! Second Throw! Drit Throw! Tornado Throw!”
Three weapons were hurled from Cola’s hands, spinning as they flew around the dragon. The three weapons interacted with each other, creating a tornado that bound the dragon.
“Gyaoooooooooo!?”
“Finish it! Chakram Shoot!”
Then, Cola threw a glowing chakram at the immobilized dragon. As if sealing the deal, the chakram flew straight for the dragon’s heart, pierced it, and vanished.
“Gya—”
With a thud, the dragon seemed to breathe its last.
“Bubu!”
“Bubububu!”
“Bubuhi!”
“Ahh, it’s our victory! We’ve conquered this dungeon now!”
They’re celebrating their victory. However, we exchanged glances. The main reason was the weapon Cola had just used.
“Air St… that’s a skill, right?”
“They were using combo skills too, and ‘throw’… that’s from the Throw-In skill, which means throwing, right?”
“But… isn’t that guy not a Hero?”
“No, look closely at their hands. Isn’t that a throwing weapon?”
I recognized it too. It’s definitely the same throwing weapon that the yandere pig used to have.
But… wasn’t that person using a sword at the adventurer’s guild?
“For now, if that thing is really a Hero, it’s best to step in and investigate.”
“Yeah. It’d be dangerous if they resist, so everyone stay back.”
“Y-yeah.”
The mole nodded on behalf of everyone. We don’t know if they’re friend or foe.
And… something feels off about this situation.
“Understood. Iwatani-dono, negotiate without provoking them as much as possible.”
“Leave it to me.”
